note: The pilot reported feeling ill about 18 minutes after takeoff, after earlier nonspecific discomfort.
The authors report severe chest symptoms seven minutes after the report of illness at about 18 minutes. Cabin altimeter indicated 22,000 ft. Odland reports no cough.
Robie et al. describe cough and chest pain about 30 minutes after departure. The same case in Odland gives no cough.
The event ended fatally roughly 12 hours after loss of consciousness. Robie uses a different time origin.
The authors give 13 hours from symptom onset to death.
Autopsy documents cerebral and pulmonary edema and an anatomically patent foramen ovale. The presence of the anatomical finding does not establish its causal role.
